title: Counter After Plus-Plus and Minus-Minus
statement:
A counter n starts at 0. You get a list ops of statements, run in order. Each one is exactly one of these four strings:

  • "++n" and "n++" both add 1 to the counter,
  • "--n" and "n--" both subtract 1.

Pre- and post-forms behave the same here because nothing reads the value in between. Return the counter's value after all statements have run.

examples.why: +1, +1, −1. The position of the operator does not change the effect.
Three decrements and one increment. The counter may go below zero.
Looking only at the first character would read "n" for both and miss them. The middle character is always the operator sign.

gen: (r, big) => { const n = big ? 100000 : r.int(1, 10); const out = []; for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) out.push(r.pick(["++n", "n++", "--n", "n--"])); return [out]; }
hints: You do not need to parse the statement. What do all four strings have in common, and where do they differ?
Every statement is three characters long, and the middle one is always the operator sign.
Add 1 when the middle character is '+', subtract 1 otherwise.

explain.intuition:
This is a tiny interpreter. In a real program n++ and ++n differ in what the expression returns, but here each statement stands alone, so both just add 1. That leaves only the sign to read.

Each string is three characters, and the middle one is always the sign: "+" in "++n" and "n++", "-" in the other two. Checking that one character is enough.
steps: For each statement, look at its middle character op[1].
Add 1 if it is '+', otherwise subtract 1.
pitfalls: Checking only the first character. It is 'n' for both post-forms, so "n--" and "n++" would look the same.
Treating the post-form as "apply after the next statement". Each statement is complete on its own.

solutions.title: Match the full statement
solutions.idea: Compare each statement against the two increment strings.

solutions.title: Read the middle character
solutions.idea: The middle character of every statement is the sign.

followups: Statements can now also be "n += 5" or "n -= 2". How would you parse them?
Return the counter's value after every statement, like a running log.
lcTitle: Final Value of Variable After Performing Operations
